questions.question: Sales are R4 500 000 and cost of sales R3 000 000. Gross profit, and the mark-up on cost, are:
Net profit before tax is R700 000. Income tax at the company rate of 27 percent is:
options: R189 000, leaving net profit after tax of R511 000
R196 000, leaving net profit after tax of R504 000
R252 000, leaving net profit after tax of R448 000

questions.question: Interest expense is R120 000 on a loan of R1 000 000. The interest rate a question may ask for is:
The correct order of the income statement chain is:
options: Operating profit, gross profit, net profit before tax, tax
Gross profit, net profit after tax, operating profit, tax
Sales, tax, gross profit, operating profit
Gross profit, operating profit, net profit before tax, net profit after tax

subtopics.title: Share Capital, Buy-backs and Retained Income

questions.question: Share capital of R2 920 000 over seven hundred and thirty thousand shares gives an average issue price of:
options: R4,00 — the key figure for any buy-back working
R4,60 — the mid-point of the two prices

questions.question: Thirty thousand shares are repurchased at R4,60 when the average issue price is R4,00. Retained income decreases by:
options: R18 000 — thirty thousand times the 60 cents above the average
Nothing — only share capital is affected

questions.question: In the same buy-back, the credit to bank is:
options: R138 000 — the full repurchase price, equal to the two debits combined

questions.question: Opening retained income R350 000, net profit after tax R511 000, dividends R328 500. The closing balance is:
options: R532 500 — and the unpaid final dividend of R182 500 also appears as a current liability

subtopics.title: Cash Flow Signposts and the Three Workings

questions.question: Tax charge R189 000; SARS owed R12 000 at the start and R18 000 at the end. Tax PAID is:
options: R183 000 — charge plus opening owed minus closing owed
R189 000 — always equal to the charge

questions.question: Last year's final dividend was R130 000, this year's interim R146 000, this year's final R182 500. Dividends PAID this year:
options: R276 000 — last year's final plus this year's interim; this year's final is still a liability

questions.question: In a Grade 12 cash flow statement, the disposal of fixed assets is recorded at:
options: Carrying value — no profit or loss on disposal is introduced at this level

questions.question: Proceeds of a new share issue appear in the cash flow statement under:
options: They do not appear, as shares are not cash
Financing activities — together with buy-backs and loan movements

subtopics.title: The Indicators That Decide the Marks

questions.question: Current assets R840 000, inventories R360 000, current liabilities R400 000. The current and acid-test ratios are:
Return on total capital employed is 20,4 percent while the loan costs 12 percent. The gearing conclusion is:
options: The loan must be repaid at once
Positive gearing — each borrowed rand earns more than it costs, so borrowing for expansion is defensible
The comparison is irrelevant to gearing

questions.question: Net asset value is about 473 cents and the shares trade at 540 cents. The 67 cents premium means:
options: The books have understated the assets by error
The market is pricing future prospects the balance sheet cannot record
The share price must fall to 473 cents

questions.question: Earnings per share 70 cents, dividends per share 45 cents. The pay-out policy is roughly:
options: 64 percent paid out — generous to income-seekers, with about a third retained for growth

subtopics.title: The Pizzeria's Year on One Page

questions.question: The pizzeria's pizzas cost R3 000 000 to make and sold for R4 500 000. The cooking itself earned:
options: R1 500 000 — every rand of cost became a rand and a half of price

questions.question: The tax collector's slice of company profit is:
options: Fifteen cents in every rand, like VAT
A fixed twenty-seven cents in every rand of profit

questions.question: Each slice earned 70 cents but was paid 45 cents. The 25 cents difference:
options: Stayed in the pizzeria as retained profit, making every slice worth more
Must be paid out next year by law

questions.question: Profit earned, profit paid and profit kept describe:
options: Sales, cost of sales and gross profit
The three sections of the cash flow statement
Earnings per share, dividends per share and retained income per share

subtopics.title: Following the Cash, Not the Profit

questions.question: The bank balance did not grow by the full profit because:
options: Profit and cash run on different clocks — some charges are unpaid and some payments settle old debts
Cash always equals profit eventually in the same year

questions.question: Of this year's R189 000 tax slice, R18 000 will only be paid next year, and R12 000 of old tax debt was settled. Cash out for tax:
The delivery scooters wearing out cost profit every year but take no cash because:
options: The mechanic is paid in cash
Depreciation is a non-cash expense — the cash left when the scooters were bought
The scooters belong to the bank

questions.question: Selling one hundred and thirty thousand new slices to cousins for R676 000 brought cash in:
options: As a loan from the cousins
Without a single pizza being cooked — a financing inflow, not profit

subtopics.title: Three Questions Before You Buy a Slice

questions.question: The books value a slice at about 473 cents but cousins pay 540 cents. The 67 cents extra buys:
options: The pizzeria's future — customers, location and next year's pizzas, which the books may not record

questions.question: The pizzeria earned 16,9 cents per rand of family money while the bank pays about 8. The extra 9 cents is:
options: The reward for the risk the family carries by investing in a business

questions.question: The whole pot earns 20,4 cents per rand and the loan costs 12. If earning power slid below 12:
options: The loan would start working against the family, because the bank collects in bad years too
The bank would convert the loan to shares

questions.question: The three-sentence habit the examination pays for on every indicator is:
options: Quote the figure, compare it to something, judge with a reason
